title: Payroll run service with signal-driven shutdown
name: Pay run service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this service shuts down on SIGTERM? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does main call srv.Shutdown before runner.Drain rather than the other way round?
choices: Once HTTP intake has stopped and handlers have returned, nothing can call Submit any more, so closing the queue in Drain cannot cut off or reject new work
srv.Shutdown must run first because it releases the port that the workers need in order to write results
Drain cancels baseCtx immediately, which would make the HTTP handlers return 500 for requests in flight
The order does not matter because Submit holds r.mu and the queue is buffered

questions.prompt: Why do Submit and Drain both take r.mu and use the closed flag?
choices: To make worker goroutines process runs one at a time in submission order
To stop Drain from being called twice by two signals arriving at once and hanging in wg.Wait
To ensure a send on r.queue can never happen after close(r.queue), which would panic
To protect the statuses map in the store from concurrent writers

questions.prompt: Suppose the shutdown context expires while two pay runs are still being processed and three more are waiting in the queue. What does the runner do with them?
choices: It discards the queued runs without recording anything, since the channel is closed
Workers keep going until every employee is paid, because Drain waits on <-done after abort
Each in-progress run is rolled back so no partial payroll lines remain in the store
Workers see the cancelled baseCtx, mark each remaining run interrupted, and Drain returns an error so the process exits non-zero
